description: Every UC must reference at least one table from the supplied schema.
Every column in High Level Design must exist exactly in the schema.
Copy table/column names exactly (catalog.schema.table and exact column identifier).
Statement and Solution each must name at least 2 backticked columns from Tables Involved.
No invented capabilities — concepts must trace to a column or be explicitly derived.
Full-portfolio signal coverage: date+measure, fact+dim FK, grouping id, status column each must produce >=1 UC.
No invented dollar/percent figures; use [ESTIMATE: depends on <column>] when quantification needed.
No near-duplicate UCs; merge UCs differing only by technique on identical Tables Involved.
No invented organizational constructs (programs/tiers/committees) without a column grounding them.
No inferred-externality claims (industry benchmarks, market prices, regulations) — must trace to a column.
Technique must be structurally supported by columns (funnel needs stages, survival needs start+end event, cohort needs onboarding ts).
No umbrella techniques (AI Analysis, Data Science, General Analytics) — use a specific technique label.
Output discipline — pure CSV only; no narration/preamble/afterword allowed.
On 2+-table schemas, >=30% of UCs must span 2+ tables via column-name-inferred joins.
where_enforced: BASE_USE_CASE_GEN_PROMPT STRUCTURAL JOIN HEURISTIC; Phase L L18_multi_table_ratio

description: Pre-emission §A: UC must identify Who funds it / What decision it changes / Who owns the outcome.
Pre-emission §B: UC must pass compute-proof / technique-data fit / data-fit sanity.
Pre-emission §C: Pattern coverage / FK exploitation / type balance / technique redundancy <=25%.
Pre-emission §D: Stakeholder plausibility — realistic beneficiary/sponsor roles; no invented programs.
Pre-emission §E: Every $/percent figure traces to a column OR is tagged [ESTIMATE: ...].
Pre-emission §F: No marketing copy; plain operational language; specific technique names.
Pre-emission §G: Within-batch dedup check before emitting any UC.
Pre-emission §I: Coherence — technique matches problem; Solution produces claimed Business Value; no topic switching; multi-table necessity.
Pre-emission §J: Self-test — same-code reproducibility; cheaper alternative check; precision vs stakes; senior-reviewer swap test.
Pre-emission §K: Portfolio smell — scoring non-compression; technique redundancy check; no wording repetition; no domain starvation; no industry self-contradiction.
Phase L L1: any UCs produced — BLOCKING if zero.
Phase L L5: every UC has Primary Table after derivation loop.
Phase L L13: schema_details present.
Phase L L14: every UC's Primary Table is grounded (matches a known schema table).
Phase L L18: multi-table ratio >=30% on 2+-table schemas.
Phase Q1 GROUNDING — drop UCs citing unknown tables.
Phase Q2 DEDUP — canonical signature merge of near-dups.
Phase Q3 RELEVANCE R1+R2 — technique structurally supported by cited columns.
Phase Q4 RECALL — detected operational patterns must be covered by at least one UC.
Gap G6 Q1d — translated UC identifiers (Primary Table / Tables Involved / result_table) must match English originals byte-for-byte.
Gap G15 — per-business lock (__inspire_lock Delta table) prevents concurrent Generate clobbering.
Gap G14 — opt-in calibration cell writes scaffold inventory JSON to /tmp/inspire_calibration.json.
Structural FK inference must handle camelCase (customerID) AND underscore (customer_id) patterns.
UC generation batches must include all tables in schemas <=20 tables (no 1-table-per-call).
Early FK inference must run before UC generation batching to populate foreign_key_graph in time.
G2 column-grounding must exclude known table names and FQN references from ungrounded list.

R6 subject-action check demoted to INFO (from DROP) due to high false-positive rate on generic prepositional nouns (per-mile/per-time/per-available); still surfaces suspects via UC_ACTION_SUBJECT_SUSPECT.
R2 technique-data fit adds column-name-stem fallback when all schema types are STRING (common in synthetic/delta-share schemas); recognizes date/time/year/amount/count/etc. as type-role proxies.
TableSizeAnalyzer DESCRIBE fallback when information_schema.columns returns 0 columns for a table (prevents silent drops from samples/delta-share catalogs).

Ultra High: the red-team verdict is derived from structured fatal_flaws (OUTCOME_DERIVED_FROM_INPUTS, NO_DECISION_CHANGED, DUPLICATE_OF_ANOTHER_USE_CASE, DATA_SHAPE_ASSUMPTION_UNVERIFIABLE, INFEASIBLE_WITH_AVAILABLE_COLUMNS, VALUE_OVERCLAIMED); a self-contradictory judge record (fatal red-team category not listed as a fatal flaw, ELITE or NEAR_MISS with a fatal flaw, a verdict better than its own scores and value tier allow) is discarded and judged again.

Ultra High: a supervised use case whose outcome is computed from its own signal columns in the same period is rejected as a rule over its inputs (label leakage or tautology); an outcome observed in a later window with a dated time column passes.

Ultra High: a co-occurrence use case grouped by its table's own row key, or a central KEY_HAS_REPEATED_ROWS runtime assumption on a row key, is rejected; every other runtime assumption becomes a readiness check of the Genie Code instruction, and the notebook stops before it builds anything when one does not hold.
Ultra High: elites that change the same decision (same canonical title, or same decision object and technique on another channel's table) collapse to the higher elite score.

One key-name rule: *_id, *_key, *_sk, *_pk, *_fk, *_nk, *_code, *_no, *_num, *_number, *_ref, *_uuid, *_guid, camelCase and concatenated forms, plus declared PK/FK columns; a text column named as the decision's entity is a natural entity key; a date key that joins a dated table is a time column (time via join).

The Genie Code instruction names one AI endpoint and tells the notebook to call ai_query with failOnError => false and without a temperature; model-technique use cases built on Databricks AI text functions without training run as family G.

Every LLM CSV answer passes one shared row guard: a row short of its required columns, a row with unexplained extra values, a non-numeric honesty score or an honesty number in a data column, or a verbatim-copied anchor (use case id, table name, technique, quality label, enum value) sitting in another column is rejected, counted per reason and treated as missing so the caller retries it; honesty columns are stripped only where the row shape proves their position.

A translation answer is truncated only when it ends inside an open quoted field, its final row stops mid-row, or the closing rows the prompt required never started; a complete answer that lacks a row is retried once with the cache bypassed and splits only if the retry is incomplete too. A dedup keep-list that was cut off is refused instead of dropping every use case after the cut.

Every grounding-sensitive prompt (combined value+quality scorer, Best-of-Best prescreen, Ultra High elite judge with its evidence repair and second opinion, and the Genie Code instruction prompt) renders every column of every table it reasons about; a per-batch table subset bounds prompt size, never column truncation, and a superset gate rebuilds any markdown that dropped a referenced column.

Launch safety: the agent and every generated notebook run one job run at a time per job (max_concurrent_runs=1, queue enabled), break self-launch recursion with the dbx_inspire_ai_child_run run-parameter marker instead of job-context detection, and refuse to start more than 20 runs per job in any 60-minute window.
where_enforced: JobLauncher.launch (max_concurrent_runs=1, queue, launch_cap, [LAUNCH-CAP FIRED]); INSPIRE_CHILD_MARKER self-launch gate

description: A run never ships an empty result: when no use case clears the selected quality bar (or no elite clears the Ultra High bar) the closest candidates are kept, each labelled below the bar with the reason, and the funnel ledger records the zero-bar fallback; a crash or a soft-accept is never substituted for the honest fallback.

Every cached LLM step keys on the exact content that determines the answer: per-call steps (generation, Best-of-Best, elite judge, domain and assignment, translation, Genie) key on the full rendered prompt, model and request params, and the combined value+quality score cache keys on the use-case set, the scoring context and the full per-batch schema payload sent, so a schema or prompt change can never replay a stale score.

A scoring batch that times out is retried, never silently dropped: only the first attempt is cut by the straggler budget, every retry gets the full per-task timeout, and a timed-out batch is retried in halves for up to scoring_split_retry_rounds rounds. An unusable answer gets one retry per use case, also when it first arrives on the retry of a timed-out batch; a second unusable answer that recovers nothing stops. A use case still unscored after every retry is reported at ERROR with its reason and counted in the funnel ledger.

Log by cause: a failure the pipeline recovers from (a worker cancelled by its own parent task, an LLM attempt that is retried or cascaded, an answer the caller re-asks for, a fallback that still completes the stage) is a WARNING, and a cancelled worker step ends ended_warning; ERROR is reserved for an outcome that degraded, such as a use case lost, a stage left on defaults or an artifact not written.

An unusable dedup keep-list (cut off, a reviewed use case outside the id column, or no reviewed id at all) is asked for once more with the LLM cache bypassed; global dedup then falls back to per-domain dedup only when that is a different request (more than one group), otherwise all use cases are kept with one ERROR; an LLM call that already failed through the model cascade is not asked again.

A single-column CSV answer (the dedup keep-list after its honesty columns are removed) is never passed through the comma-based preamble rule, so a trailing note can never delete the kept ids; the id column of an answer without a header is the column most rows put a reviewed id in, so one commentary line cannot move it.

The elite-judge prompt names every key its parser reads, including verdict and scores. A record that is discarded (an invalid verdict, a missing key or a self-contradiction) is re-judged with the exact reason and the allowed verdicts, and the log names the rejected value; a verdict still above what its own scores and value tier support after that re-judge is capped at the supported verdict, keeping the original in verdict_capped_from.

Every customer-data read lives in DeepEvidence and reads aggregates only, in both Discovery Types. Standard Discovery uses those aggregates only to decide each use case: InspireAIGate withholds every measured number from every AI prompt and restores it in the reply, so the AI sees metadata only.

AI Enhanced Discovery also shows the aggregates to the AI (row counts, null share, distinct counts, date ranges, short value lists of non-personal low-cardinality columns, join match rates, KPI baselines); no data row is ever sent and data_access.rows_sent_to_ai is always 0. Every statement is logged and bounded by the deep_* time and count budgets; a table that cannot be read stays unread.
The values of a personal column (matched by name or by a PII tag) are never read: it gets counts only, no value list, no first or last date and no MIN or MAX KPI.

Goals, priorities, strategy entries, KPIs, key results and sponsors never reach generation, the quality checks, the 19 gates, Best-of-Best or the elite judge; before selection Value is ROI x 0.80 + Time to Value x 0.10 + Reusability x 0.10, computed by Inspire.
Every strategy alignment cites the use case's own columns or KPI; an alignment without that evidence, or to an unknown entry id, is dropped and the use case is Not aligned.

The strategy never adds, keeps or rescues a use case: the alignment pass runs on the final use cases only and the agent raises an error if the set changes. User-domain coverage and the feedback exclusion run before it.

Money amounts, percentages, multipliers and counts in KPIs, key results, measures and benefits come only from the user's strategy, priorities or business context or from a measured Deep baseline; any other figure is replaced with a labeled placeholder.

The LLM never writes SQL that Inspire executes: KPI queries are built only by DeepEvidence.kpi_sql from validated specs (allowlisted aggregates over existing columns of the use case's tables or a real metric view measure, filters only on observed values, quoted identifiers).
Every LLM call attempt is written exactly once to _ailogs in Semunity's design (agent = inspire): one row per attempt, a terminal exhausted row when no attempt succeeded, no row for a cache hit.

A log write never fails or delays an LLM call: rows are spooled and inserted in byte-capped chunks, a failing chunk is retried and quarantined after 5 tries (a permission error is never retried, see R109), and without an inspire database rows go to ailogs.jsonl.

A CSV header line longer than 400 characters is still found when every field is a short column name, so a wide translation header is never stripped as prose; long prose lines before the CSV are still removed.
A strategy entry with KPIs that no aligned use case computes is never an alignment: its use cases are re-aligned once without it, leftover alignments to it are removed, and it is reported as a gap.

A strategy KPI about a physical quantity (emissions, energy, mass, volume, distance, temperature) keeps its kpi_id only when the computation's column, measure or filter names that quantity; otherwise the link, name and unit are removed.
Data foundations are anchored on fact tables (a child of a kept foreign key and nobody's parent) with the dimensions they join; shared dimensions never merge facts into one foundation.
The translation payload lists its keys in the CSV header's column order, pinned by a test to the prompt header, so translated values never shift columns.
The [AILOGS CHECK] self-check runs before the end-of-run log capture in every run, with or without an inspire database, and runs once.

Each business priority a final use case serves raises its Strategic Alignment by 0.25, for at most 2 priorities and never past 5, so priorities move the final order; they never add, keep or remove a use case.

A rate, share or ratio KPI is computed by the KPI builder as numerator / denominator on one table; a KPI whose name claims a rate or a model output its computation does not produce is renamed, and a strategy KPI computed another way is kept as a marked proxy.

A workspace path given without the /Workspace prefix (a relative generation path resolved next to the notebook, or a /Shared, /Users or /Repos path) is used in its /Workspace form, so a run whose identity cannot write the vol_root volume of the inspire database streams its live log under the generation path; a disabled live log names the reason for each target.

The strict JSON response format wraps the array that grading and alignment prompts return in an object with a results array, the only root endpoints accept, and the startup check allows the endpoint 128 output tokens to write it; a strict answer that is not that array, or a rejected response format or schema, falls back to the plain request on that endpoint and is never treated as a prompt that is too long; the check waits at most 20 seconds, and the run log names for every checked endpoint whether strict JSON is on and why it is off.

A ratio KPI whose numerator equals its denominator is not computable; a % unit is kept only for a share (COUNT over COUNT, COUNT_DISTINCT over COUNT or COUNT_DISTINCT, SUM over SUM), otherwise the percent is dropped and the KPI is renamed or kept as a marked proxy; a KPI filter is kept unless the data evidence lists every value of its column and the value is not one of them, in which case the KPI is not computable.

A use case the user rejected stays out of later runs for the same business when the next run proposes it again reworded: a candidate on the same primary table whose subject (the words before "with") shares at least 60% and whose title shares at least 50% of their words with the rejected title is excluded and logged with both scores; a shared deliverable alone never matches.

A Genie Code regeneration (Generate Use Cases, Route 1 or Route 2) that writes none of the flagged notebooks fails the run with a failed step and the first write error; a partial one ends with a warning step and completes with warnings that count the notebooks not written.
The [AILOGS CHECK] non-success rate counts model calls only; failed ENDPOINT_PROBE requests are reported apart, so a workspace with unusable endpoints does not fail the check.

Generate Use Cases holds the business's Generate lock per run, not per session: a second Genie regeneration that finds the lock held by another live run records a failed step and stops, so two jobs of one session never regenerate the same use cases; a lock that cannot be read or written still lets the run proceed with a recorded failed step.

When the catalog holds more than N use cases, the run stars up to N of them as Best of Best (a smaller catalog is already the short list and nothing is starred): N comes from 16_best_of_best_count, else from the generation instructions, else 20, and 0 stars none. Only a use case that passed every elite test (value tier, the four dimensions at 8 or more, verified columns and joins, the red team, a second opinion for a near miss) can be starred; the highest elite scores win, the best passing use case of each user business domain first, and no domain takes more than max(2, ceil(N x 0.25)) stars while other domains still have passing use cases. Fewer passing use cases star fewer, with no padding. Marking never changes membership, scores or order; Ultra High reuses the selection's verdicts.

The stratified trim keeps each theme's best use case by Best-of-Best score and gives the remaining slots to the strongest remaining use cases across all themes, never above the per-theme cap; slots are never handed out by theme size, so a large theme of weak use cases cannot push out strong use cases of small themes.

An endpoint whose startup probe did not finish stays in the model list but follows every endpoint that passed its probe, in every cascade; the reorder is logged as [LLM_ENDPOINT_PROBE_ORDER FIRED] and an endpoint the probe never reached keeps its place.

Generation keeps a use case only when its decision moves revenue, cost or loss directly, moves a line of the Revenue Model, a Value Chain step or the Strategic Initiative of the business context, or automates manual work; the generation criteria carry no strategy wording and no extra risk criterion.

The trim target (target_max_use_cases plus a draw from 1 to target_max_jitter) is drawn from the session id, so re-running a session ships the same catalog size and new sessions still vary across the range.

A Genie Code notebook has three cells written by Inspire: a markdown cell with the title, the Best of Best line for a starred use case, a short use-case card, a one-line disclaimer and the line that tells the user to copy the cell below into Genie Code without its surrounding triple quotes and let Genie Code implement it; the instruction as a raw-string code cell (unverified names first, KPIs and KPI queries appended); and the Run controls cell, always the last cell. The instruction stands on its own: it names every table, column, join, threshold, the business output table with its columns and the model it may register, and the notebook writes nothing when a readiness check or the acceptance rule fails.

A proposed key result, benefit or measure of success with an unindexed [BASELINE] takes the baseline of the KPI it names; a key result that names no KPI, in a use case with several KPIs, keeps the pending text. Deep KPI baselines are measured for the first KPI of every use case before any second KPI, and baselines skipped by the distinct-query cap are logged.

One call names the idea themes of all Best-of-Best-scored use cases from one shared list, and the scoring prompt names none; only ids the call was sent and themes of at most 6 words are applied, spellings that differ only in case are merged, use cases the answer leaves out go to a second call that sees the themes already used, an answer with fewer than min(8, n/6) themes is retried once without the cache, and without a usable answer each use case takes its subdomain as its theme.

A parallel wait longer than a minute writes one [WAIT-HEARTBEAT] line a minute to the run log with its step (the executor context's name, the task name, or the label of a split-retry scoring stage), the tasks done and in progress, and the time elapsed against the step's limit; every wait on an executor context goes through its named wait; a single model call longer than a minute writes its Still waiting line to the run log at DEBUG once a minute.

The instruction's Parameters section lists every widget the Genie notebook creates first: the core widgets from the use case spec (business output table, the model for the patterns that register one, AI endpoint, as-of date, forecast horizon and season length for forecasts, tier shares, explanation count and every readiness and acceptance threshold) with the code's defaults, plus at most 6 use-case widgets, each with a default, each created with its used-for text as the label; a core default the model changed is restored and a widget without a default is dropped.

Every Genie instruction ends with a Platform Rules section written by code: the serverless rule the prompt and AGENTS.md share, the Spark Connect DECIMAL rule, the cast of every business output column before the write to its contract type (an existing table of another type is converted once, see R123), and for the patterns that register a model the MLflow 2 logging call of serverless environment 4 (artifact_path, never name), with the new version taken from the returned model info because Unity Catalog rejects a run_id filter in search_model_versions.

A group comparison stops only when fewer than min_reportable_groups groups hold at least min_group_rows rows; smaller groups are left out of the findings and counted, never a reason to stop the run; a group is the unit the findings compare and report (a store, category, segment, tier or period), and the entities a Pareto, a network or a ranking scores are rows inside the groups, never groups themselves (in Genie round 18 a Pareto counted store-item pairs and a network counted single senders as groups, and both stopped with 0 reportable groups).

The instruction's data section says how nulls in each signal, rating or outcome column are handled: left out and counted, or carried with a data_quality_flag reason, never filled with an invented value.

A star candidate that passed every elite test but was removed as a duplicate or a decision twin carries the reason the dropping step recorded; drop reasons name the kept use case by title, never by an id the final renumbering changes.

Foreign keys inferred from column names strip leading role words ending in ed or ing as well as parts of at most 4 characters; any other longer leading word blocks the match, so a compound entity name such as order_item_id is never read as a key of item.
A recommendation notebook fits on all past interactions; eligibility rules such as margin, stock or items already bought apply only when ranking, never before fitting.

Every Genie notebook has an as_of_date widget whose default latest means the last period complete in every event-facts table the features and the outcome read (the earliest of those tables' newest dates; entity and reference tables do not count); every window, holdout, period grid and scoring population ends at it, a forecast's period grid never runs past the data, and the staleness stop names the max_staleness_cadences widget as the way to forecast from older data.
An optimization or simulation notebook draws from aggregates computed once before the draw loop, never from a scan of the source rows inside it.

Readiness counts are taken on the joined source rows inside the windows before any feature engineering; row_count counts rows of the primary table whose entity key and time column are present, a missing feature never removes a row from a readiness count, and a failed check prints how many rows each filter removed; after feature engineering a second check counts the rows each fit, holdout and scoring step receives, and an empty one fails with how many rows each feature's nulls removed.

A Genie notebook contains every build step, fully written, including the business output write and the summary step, the last step run_use_case() runs, even when a run stops at readiness or acceptance; a stop skips that work and never removes or stubs it, and the definition of done requires every step fully written and none stubbed.

The acceptance rule is exactly the one Inspire states for the execution pattern, never extended by the instruction, and what an acceptance failure does is rendered per pattern: the model patterns print No approved model yet, register no model and write the baseline's rows, a forecast publishes the seasonal naive forecast, a group comparison never stops and makes findings that are not significant Monitor, AI text processing stops above max_ai_error_rate and writes nothing, and an optimization prints No better plan found and writes the current plan.

Every Genie instruction carries the platform rule that no fit, score, forecast, simulation or ai_query step is ever called on an empty input: the notebook counts the rows the step receives and, when there are none, prints how many rows each filter and each feature removed and stops by the stop rule; when a step or a model wrapper splits its input by a key or a model type, each empty slice is skipped instead of calling the model on it (in Genie round 20 a model wrapper called scikit-learn on an empty model-type slice).

A recommendation notebook never uses Spark ML ALS, which serverless compute rejects (UC_COMMAND_NOT_SUPPORTED: Unity Catalog does not support the higher-order functions it runs), even when the use case's design names it; the implementation guidance names item-item similarity or truncated SVD with scikit-learn and scipy, and the work stays sparse: only each item's top neighbors are kept, users are scored in batches keeping each user's top items, and no dense items-by-items or users-by-items matrix is built.

A permission error on an Inspire step or AI call log table is permanent: the writer stops sending that table's rows after one [SPOOL-DENIED FIRED] warning that names the table and the local spool that keeps the rows, the live log streamer copies the AI call log spool next to the live log as ailogs.jsonl, and the run-end [AILOGS CHECK] fails rows_reach_the_table when the table refused or quarantined rows.

The Run controls cell carries the JobLauncher and an Execution widget that defaults to As job: running the notebook creates or updates its persistent job dbx_inspire_ai_<slug>_<hash8> (one concurrent run, queued, a paused schedule at the decision cadence) tagged dbx_inspire_ai_business, dbx_inspire_ai_usecase, dbx_inspire_ai_session_id, dbx_inspire_ai_launcher_source, dbx_inspire_ai_run_type and dbx_inspire_ai_notebook, runs it with the notebook's widget values and dbx_inspire_ai_child_run = 1, and waits for it. In the job run and with Execution = Here, inspire_main() runs run_use_case() in place, a launch that fails runs it in place with a note that the run is not tagged, and the instruction tells Genie Code to keep the cell, test with Here and set As job again at the end.

A key column is never a free-text column: _column_signals excludes key-like names (_sk, _id, _code and the other key suffixes) from text_cols, so a text word inside a key name (reason_sk, review_id) never makes an ai_query that annotates a numeric result count as AI text processing, never moves a model use case to execution family G, never fails the elite verification for citing no free-text column, and never passes the Q3 text check for a text technique.

In Good and High mode every use case that passes every elite test in the Best of Best stage keeps the judge's verified assessment in elite_assessment, without elite_status or elite_score, so the tracking row persists it, a Route 1 regeneration reloads it, the Genie notebook card shows its decision, owner, cadence and KPI, and its job gets a paused schedule at that cadence; failed or unjudged use cases keep none, and the Good and High exports keep their columns.

A Genie notebook carries no use case details table: its short card (R140) holds what the person copying the instruction needs, and the full use case details stay in the catalog artifacts and the App; a skeleton notebook, which has no card, keeps every row of the use case details table.

Every elite judge call of a run starts on one pinned endpoint: the first healthy endpoint of elite_judge_preferred_endpoints (default databricks-claude-opus-4-8, the model the elite bars were calibrated on), else the first healthy endpoint of the judge cascade; another endpoint becomes the judge only after the pinned one is demoted or unusable ([ELITE-JUDGE-PINNED FIRED]), and the second opinion comes from the first healthy endpoint other than the pinned judge.

When no table name matches a key column's stem, foreign key inference compares the stem with each table's own key column (named after the table or a word of it once its short prefix is removed): an exact stem, a stem whose one or two extra leading letters start the target's column prefix, or a stem of three or more letters that abbreviates the key; the target must be unique, use the same key token and type family, and a table's own key never links to another table.

The coverage catch-all keeps an unused master or reference table when a declared or inferred foreign key path joins it to a transactional table (the shared join-path contract, up to 4 hops) or when it shares a key-like column name with one; the bridge tables on that path are sent with the retry batch and named in its instruction, and a table nothing joins is still excluded.

The run's known tables (global_table_names and the generation validator's schema) include the tables the table filter classified as REFERENCE, and every table a generation call sent to the model counts as known for that call; a use case is rejected as hallucinated only for a table that is in neither.

Phase L's production-readiness check (J3) and the G2 grounding check share one rule for backticked identifiers: a schema column (of the cited tables for G2, of the schema for J3), a known table name, bare or fully qualified, or a SQL keyword is grounded; J3 fails a use case only for 3 or more backticked names that are none of these.

Every 'Act now' or 'Review' row of a Genie Code notebook's business output carries its own next step after its tier's text, from a fixed template the instruction defines and the row's computed facts fill; the action target is the elite assessment's decision, else the deliverable after the last 'with' in the use case name, never a generic phrase.

Priority tiers follow each row's evidence: 'Act now' and 'Review' go to the top-ranked rows that pass the use case's decision test, which a row whose expected impact is a loss never passes, and a row whose data_quality_flag is not 'ok' is Monitor; rank orders by expected impact (the value times the row's exposure) when the method gives both; data_quality_flag carries only the row's own input problems, and run-level notes go to the summary cell.

A significance test runs on observed values with seasonality handled inside the test (season indicators in an OLS over the full history, or each period against the same period a cycle earlier), never on a smoothed or fitted series and never after an STL decomposition, with HAC standard errors only from 30 points; it uses a library test from statsmodels or scipy, never a hand-written test statistic, allows for autocorrelation in a time series, corrects for multiple tests and prints how many series it flags in each direction, and when it flags every tested series each row says so in data_quality_flag. The rule reaches both the model that writes the instruction and Genie Code.

Each acting row's explanation prompt is built in pandas as one text column from the facts the code computed and formatted (entity label, value with its unit, top reasons and the main driver or cause); the ai_query SQL reads only that column and adds no facts, the prompt asks the model only to word them in plain text, without responseFormat and with failOnError => false as a named argument, never named_struct('failOnError', false), which ai_query does not read as that option and then returns plain text (Genie round 14), the struct ai_query returns is stored as its result text, the prompt column stays out of the business output, and the model never chooses a driver, cause, rank or number; a prompt assembled in SQL with CAST(value AS STRING) put 0.6793932502246776 into 4 of 4 explanations in Genie round 12. The summary step's ai_query prompt is built the same way, from facts the code computed and formatted, never a raw number, dict or list: each number covers the rows its fact names, a group whose key is missing is named for what it is ('no carrier'), never 'nan' or 'None', and the step raises an error before the call when the prompt holds 'unknown', 'nan', 'None' or 'inf'. In Genie round 36 the freight summary paired each carrier's alert count with its excess freight over all of its lines, so the Transportation Manager read that the queue's 19 alerts came with total excess freight of 1,136K, its first summary named a missing carrier 'nan', and the Pareto summary read 'scored 60897 store-items'.

Keys, ids, ranks and counts stay integers, or strings when they can be null, through pandas and Spark Connect, and only Decimal values are cast to float, and numpy values become Python types before json.dumps or dbutils.notebook.exit, which reject numpy booleans and numbers (a numpy bool in an exit payload failed a round 15 notebook), and DATE values, which arrive as Python datetime.date objects in pandas columns and from first() or collect(), are converted with pd.to_datetime before a comparison, Timedelta arithmetic or a Timestamp method (a date compared with a Timestamp failed a round 17 notebook, and .date() on a newest date read with first() failed a round 20 notebook), and because Spark never mixes BOOLEAN and numbers a 0/1 flag is cast to BOOLEAN before OR or AND and a BOOLEAN to INT before SUM or arithmetic (an OR of two coalesced flags failed a round 20 notebook); a business output table whose existing column type differs from the contract type is converted once and rewritten with the contract types instead of being followed; a contract column the table lacks is added, NULL for older rows, and a column the contract does not list is kept, NULL in the new rows, with its name printed, because a user may have added it (in Genie round 13 a legacy extra column made Genie Code rewrite the table and rerun); every business output column is built on the working frame and pandas NaN becomes None only in the copy made for the write, so the summary step keeps the frame's columns and types (in round 14 a converted working frame made rank an object column and the summary cell failed, and in round 20 metadata columns added only to the write copy broke a summary preview).

An acceptance failure still writes rows where a sound fallback exists: a model pattern writes the baseline's rows with method set to the baseline, scored by the baseline model for every entity of the scoring population (a constant such as the class rate is only the reference it is compared with and is never written as value; in Genie round 16 every row carried the class rate), registers no model and makes every row Monitor when the baseline also misses the thresholds; an optimization writes the current plan, every row Monitor; a forecast publishes the seasonal naive forecast; a group comparison makes findings that are not significant Monitor. Data freshness only flags rows ('data ends <newest date>') and never stops the run. AI text above the error-rate limit still writes nothing.

The 20,000-character instruction target measures the model's draft, not the Platform Rules Inspire appends, so a draft goes back for length only when the model can shorten it, and the repair log names the length reason.

Every number written into top_reasons, recommended_action or an ai_query prompt is formatted first by one Python function: 3 significant figures, a K, M or B suffix for large amounts and '< 0.001' for smaller p- and q-values, never a raw double or scientific notation (so never Python's g format), and never turned into text inside SQL, where CAST, concat and format_string write the raw double; pandas frames are named *_pdf and Spark frames *_sdf and move between the two only through toPandas() and spark.createDataFrame(...).

Seasonal data is compared with the same season of earlier cycles, never with an all-season average: Cohort Analysis compares each cohort with the prior cohorts that started in the same season at the same offset and leaves out the cohort of the data's first period, whose members may predate the data; Trend Analysis tests the observed values minus the STL seasonal component, never the STL trend.

Serverless has no cache, so a Genie Code notebook runs each expensive step (a model fit per group, an ai_query call, a large join) in one Spark action, collects its small result to pandas and takes later counts and checks from that pandas frame; a recomputed lineage re-ran 495 model fits on every action in Genie round 7.

A trend or level test leaves out the latest periods of an event that follows another by a lag (a return after its sale, a claim after its policy), which are still incomplete; in Genie round 8 every warehouse showed a significant year-over-year drop in returns because the last weeks' returns had not arrived.

Work on thousands of entities is vectorized (numpy, pandas or Spark), never a Python loop that filters, builds or sorts a frame per entity: the rows are grouped once and each entity is looked up (in Genie round 20 a Pareto's halo lookup filtered the basket frame once per item and ran past 33 minutes); a ranking is evaluated on a seeded sample of at most 5,000 entities when there are more (the sample is for the evaluation only; the scoring and the business output keep every entity, and in Genie round 16 a sample taken before the split left 306 of about 28,000 customers to score; a per-group sample uses groupby(key).sample or .head, which keep the group key, never groupby(...).apply, which dropped sm_type in round 21), the recommender scores users in batches with np.argpartition on each batch's scores converted to a dense array with .toarray() first, because np.argpartition does not take a sparse matrix, a value several steps use is computed once in the Parameters cell, each fact table is aggregated to the entity and period before it is joined, and more than 50 independent series are fitted or scored in parallel with groupBy(...).applyInPandas(...).

A business output row's entity_label is a readable name from a name or description column, or the entity key, with a period written as its name rather than a sequence number, and never contact details such as an email address, phone number or street address.

A Genie Code notebook decides which periods are complete from each source table's own dates before any filter, so a filter never makes a partial period look complete, and drops rows without an entity key or time value from the frame every later step uses, not only from the readiness count; period starts and ends come from pandas periods (pd.Period, pd.offsets) or the date table's own period columns, never from months added to a date by hand (in Genie round 20 a quarter end computed that way raised 'month must be in 1..12' for Q4).

The run waits for the business context and the generation-instruction interpretation up to CONTEXT_INIT_TIMEOUT_S (1,800 s), longer than the model cascade those calls run, so a slow first endpoint falls back instead of being cancelled; a business context that still does not arrive becomes an empty context ([CONTEXT-INIT-TIMEOUT FIRED]) and the run continues, while a generation-instruction timeout stays an error because the user's instructions are never dropped. A 300 s wait ended U18's first attempt when databricks-claude-opus-5-5 did not answer.

Spark rejects a window function inside an aggregate, an aggregate inside another aggregate and COUNT(DISTINCT ...) over a window, so a Genie Code notebook computes the window or the inner aggregate in its own step and then aggregates its result; an entropy feature that nested a window in an aggregate failed the first run of a Genie round 12 notebook, and a distinct count over a window failed the first run of a Pareto in round 19; in PySpark every comparison is parenthesized before & or |, which bind tighter than == and > (in round 21 an unparenthesized readiness filter failed a Pareto). A list of conditions is combined with functools.reduce(operator.and_, conditions) or operator.or_, never with Python's and, or, all() or any() or NumPy's logical_and, which call bool() on a Column: in Genie round 34 the lapse notebook filtered on np.logical_and.reduce over its covariates' isNotNull() conditions, and its first run raised CANNOT_CONVERT_COLUMN_INTO_BOOL. The condition of F.when is a Column, F.when(F.col('closed'), value), never a column name, and a condition written as SQL text goes through F.expr: in Genie round 35 the gift-sender notebook wrote F.when('closed', ...) for two outcome columns, and its first run raised NOT_COLUMN. The rows that meet a condition are counted with F.count_if(condition), which gives 0 when none do, never F.sum(condition.cast('int')) or F.sum(F.when(condition, 1)), which give NULL when the condition is NULL on every row of a group: in Genie round 36 the Pareto notebook's halo count was NULL for a store-item on which every comparison was NULL, and int() on it raised TypeError.

A Genie Code notebook clears attrs on every frame toPandas() returns, because Spark Connect stores the query's metrics there and pandas copies them into every row iterrows() yields, and it builds row text with vectorized column operations or itertuples(), never iterrows(); in Genie round 12 such loops ran 39 minutes over 28,447 rows and 23 minutes over 9,968 rows, while the same loop on a frame without those attrs takes under a second. itertuples() renames a column whose name starts with an underscore or is not a valid identifier to its position, so such columns get plain names first (in round 20 row._excess_cost failed a freight notebook), and pandas columns are read and assigned as x_pdf['name'], never x_pdf.name, because a column named like a DataFrame method (rank, count, tail, size) returns the method (in round 20 x_pdf.tail failed a Pareto).

When more than a quarter of the idea themes of a portfolio of 20 or more use cases hold one use case, those use cases go to one more theme call, without the cache, that lists only the themes two or more use cases share; the new placement is kept only when it leaves fewer use cases alone, and a failed call keeps the first answer. On U19, 53 of 95 themes held one use case, so the trim's one-per-theme floor kept 95 of its 110 slots whatever their score; U13, U14 and U17 had 3 or 4 such themes and are never asked again.

A Genie Code notebook prints the distribution of every weight computed from the data that shapes value or eligibility (a margin, a price, a capacity) before using it; a weight that is zero, negative or the same for most rows never multiplies, clips or filters value or the candidates, the ranking keeps the rows by the method's own score, the summary says so, and the decision test, not an eligibility filter, fails the rows whose expected impact is a loss, so the notebook still writes its ranked rows, every row Monitor when every row is a loss (in round 15 a positive-margin filter left one eligible item, every value was 1.0 and the notebook wrote nothing); before the write it checks that value varies across rows. In Genie round 13 a unit margin that is negative for all 18,000 TPC-DS items, clipped to 0, made all 454,360 recommendation values 0 and put loss-making offers in Act now.

A business output row's run_id is a uuid4 the first step of run_use_case() makes once per run of the use case and writes on every row, never the MLflow run id, which exists only when a model is logged; in Genie round 14 a recommender that registered no model wrote 454,490 rows with a NULL run_id, and in round 16 the instruction model shortened the column list to `run_id`, so the rule is also in the Platform Rules.

A runtime assumption in a Genie Code readiness check is measured on the rows its statement is about: an assumption about order lines, transactions or events is counted in the fact table that holds them, through the join path, never in a dimension table where each key appears once; in Genie round 18 an assumption about order lines per lane was counted on the 20-row ship_mode table and stopped a freight audit that had the data it needed.

The use-case card of a Genie Code notebook is short: the title, the Best of Best line for a starred use case, and a table of at most five rows (What it does; Decision with its owner and cadence, and KPI with its direction, each only when the elite assessment found it and never as a 'not assessed' placeholder; Data, the tables read; Output, the business output table), then the one-line disclaimer and then the copy line, so the line right above the instruction cell tells the user what to copy. The full use case details stay in the catalog artifacts and the App.

The Run controls cell is the last cell of a Genie Code notebook and its last line is inspire_main(): inspire_main() runs run_use_case() once, in the session when Execution is Here and in the notebook's tagged Databricks job when it is As job, and before Genie Code has defined run_use_case() it prints that nothing ran and launches no job. Genie Code adds its cells between the instruction and the Run controls, puts each build step in a function that run_use_case() runs in order, and runs only imports, function definitions and the Parameters widgets at top level, so running the whole notebook never runs the work twice and every run of the use case goes through the launcher. A value computed from the data, such as as_of_date = latest, is resolved by the first step of run_use_case(), never in the Parameters cell, because every top-level statement runs in the session and again in the job run (in Genie round 20 two notebooks queried each table's newest date in the Parameters cell).

A Genie Code notebook whose execution pattern has the min_positives threshold trains a classifier only on rows that hold at least min_positives examples of each class, and otherwise prints the class counts and stops by the stop rule; only the patterns that have that widget get the rule. In Genie round 19 an uplift notebook trained on a window with no positive outcome and wrote 9,819 rows with one value.

A Generate Use Cases run on a session that already has a row in __inspire_session attaches to it: the run only updates last_updated, so the row keeps the Discover run's results_json, inspire_json, settings, create_at and completed_on; a run that cannot read the row treats it as present, and a last_updated write that fails is a warning, never a failed run. A Discover run, or a Generate run without a row, writes the row as before. In the v1.3.0 tests four sessions lost their results this way, among them the U20 release session, whose Discover results (1.65 MB in its docs JSON) became a 1,240-character payload, so the App's Results page lost the domains, strategy coverage, foundations and stars of that session.

A Generate Use Cases run writes its live log, its AI call log copy and its docs log under run-stamped names (log_generate_<UTC yyyymmdd_HHMMSS>.log, ailogs_generate_<stamp>.jsonl, docs/generation_log_generate_<stamp>.txt) beside the Discover run's log.log, ailogs.jsonl and docs/generation_log.txt, which keep their names; a regeneration used to overwrite the Discover run's logs.

run_use_case() in a Genie Code notebook returns the run's outcome as a dict, status written with rows_written, as_of_date and run_id, or status stopped with the STOP RULE message; inspire_main() prints it in every run, the tagged job run returns it with dbutils.notebook.exit, and the notebook that launched the job reports it ('wrote N row(s) for as_of_date D with run_id R' or 'stopped without writing: <reason>'), or says the job run returned no outcome, never a blanket success. Genie Code checks each test run by that outcome, and the definition of done checks the rows with this run's run_id. In Genie round 22 a job run that stopped at its STOP RULE was reported as finished successfully, and Genie Code took an earlier run's 53,123 rows as its own.

When a Genie Code notebook computes a test, rate or mean once per unit (an item, a sender, a store) and no readiness threshold sets that unit's minimum, the minimum sample comes from the test: the smallest sample at which either of its two extreme outcomes reaches the significance level divided by the number of units with at least that sample, the level at which one unit passes the multiple-test correction on its own, and at least 5. Readiness prints how many units reach it; units below it are not tested, stay out of the multiple-test correction and keep their rows, flagged and Monitor; a test left with no unit to test never stops the run; and a unit's rate or mean is shrunk toward its baseline by its sample size before it shapes value or the rank. The model writing the instruction reads the rule too. In Genie round 22 a halo test's minimum of 30 tickets per item stopped a Pareto run with 53,999 items unwritten, and senders with one recipient ranked above every sender that could be tested. In Genie round 31 the uncorrected level gave a store-item notebook a minimum of 6 tickets, so 49,803 items with a median of 10 tickets were tested and every q-value was 1, since one item needed 21 tickets to pass a correction over 49,803 tests on its own.

A Genie Code notebook computes every ratio of columns so that a zero divisor gives NULL: serverless runs Spark SQL in ANSI mode, where dividing by zero, an invalid cast or an overflow raises an error, so a ratio is F.try_divide(a, b) (try_divide in SQL) or F.when(b != 0, a / b), text is cast with try_cast, and a pandas inf becomes NaN before a fit, a score or the write. In Genie round 23 a shipping-cost ratio over a zero column raised DIVIDE_BY_ZERO and Genie Code had to rerun.

A share, a cumulative share or a concentration (a Pareto curve, a Gini, a top-k share) in a Genie Code notebook uses values of one sign: when its measure can be negative, such as a profit, the notebook prints how many groups have a positive and how many a negative total, analyzes a group with a negative total on its losses and a group with a positive total on its positive values, counts the rows of the other sign as zero in that share and says which in each row's reason; no group is left out, and no test is left with no group, because of the sign of its measure. The model writing the instruction reads the rule too. In Genie round 23 only 2 of 700 store and class groups made a profit, and a profit Pareto that kept only those gave one q-value to all 4,979 rows it tested.

The implementation guidance of every group-comparison pattern (driver, cohort, trend, correlation, Pareto, funnel, AI, geospatial and network analysis) says what the readiness rules do: groups below the minimum rows are left out of the findings and counted, and only fewer reportable groups than min_reportable_groups, or fewer periods than min_periods, stop the run; every item of a Pareto and every node of a network stays inside its group, and every stage of a funnel keeps its conversion. The forecast guidance says stale data flags every row and never stops the run. The guidance said that contributors, nodes and other units below the minimum rows stop the run, the way a Pareto and a gifting network stopped in Genie round 18 when they applied the group minimum to every item and every sender.

A Genie Code notebook builds each per-group or per-unit result frame from an explicit column list, so a step left with no group to report still returns its columns and the join back gives NULL instead of a KeyError; calls reset_index(drop=True) right after a step that adds rows (pd.concat, explode, a landmark or window expansion) and lines up labels, predictions and features by key columns or position, never by index labels; and reads in each step only the columns the step before it returns. In Genie rounds 22 and 23 a landmark expansion duplicated a survival notebook's index, a holdout filter read a column added later, a readiness CTE dropped the date key a later join read, and a concentration test with no group to test failed with KeyError.

A Genie Code notebook that labels or compares an outcome observed over a horizon (scoring, survival, uplift, cohort and funnel analysis) chooses its training, holdout and baseline windows by whether the window is closed, meaning its last day plus the horizon is before as_of_date, never by which units already have an outcome; a unit whose horizon is still open is censored, scored or left out and never labeled a negative, and a cohort offset or funnel stage the data has not reached stays out of every comparison instead of counting as zero. The model writing the instruction reads the rule too. Inspire's guidance used closed window 9 times without defining it, and in Genie round 24 a lapse-timing notebook took the newest quarter with any closed spell as its holdout, which held only reorders, so the run stopped with nothing written. A closed window with no event is a negative, 0: over a frame that holds no rows, F.sum, F.max, F.min and F.avg return NULL while F.count returns 0, so the outcome is F.coalesce(F.sum(x).over(w), F.lit(0)) > 0 or F.count(x).over(w) > 0, and a NULL outcome marks only a censored unit. In Genie round 33 the coupon-uplift instruction labeled reorders with F.sum(...).over(w) > 0, which is NULL over a closed window with no order, and Genie Code repaired it after its second run.

A Genie Code notebook logs its model with keyword arguments only, mlflow.sklearn.log_model(sk_model=...) or mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(python_model=...) with artifact_path, signature, input_example and registered_model_name, because the first positional parameter of mlflow.pyfunc.log_model is artifact_path. Inspire's own rule showed log_model(model, artifact_path=...), and in Genie round 24 a pyfunc wrapper passed that way raised got multiple values for argument artifact_path and Genie Code had to rerun.

When Genie Code writes a notebook as a source file, every cell starts after its own # COMMAND ---------- line and that line stays directly above the Run controls title, so Genie Code's code and the Run controls never share a cell; after each import Genie Code checks that the last cell is the Run controls cell, starting with its title and ending with inspire_main(). The sentence is written once and used in the Platform Rules and in AGENTS.md. In Genie round 24 a network notebook dropped the separator above Run controls, so its 572-line last cell held both its code and the Run controls.

Each step of a Genie Code notebook keeps every column a later step reads, the keys and measures of a filter, a join, a grouping, a flag, a reason or the output, not only those of a filter, join or grouping. In Genie round 24 a feature step dropped the demographic key the output's quality flag read, and the run failed with a KeyError on cd_demo_sk until Genie Code restored it.

A Genie Code regeneration (Generate Use Cases) that finds nothing to regenerate fails the run and names why: no use case of its session or business is flagged, the Route 1 scan of the tracking table failed (with its error), no notebook under the generation path is marked, marked notebooks need an Inspire database, or they match no tracking row, and how many notebook reads or tracking lookups failed. A failed Route 1 scan or a failed notebook read is a failed step, so a run that still regenerates marked notebooks completes with warnings. It extends R83, which covered only runs with flagged rows: the first round 23 regeneration found 0 flagged use cases and ended SUCCESS, and a failed scan read as nothing flagged.

A Discover run that finds nothing to analyze, because the UC metadata lists no table with columns or every table could not be loaded, fails the run and names the metadata it read and each table not loaded with its reason. It used to log a warning and return, so the job ended SUCCESS and the session was finalized complete with no use case.

A Genie Code window over earlier or later dates, such as the features of an anchor from the orders strictly before its date or an outcome in the days after it, is a range frame on the date as a day number (rangeBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, -1) for the earlier dates, rangeBetween(1, horizon_days) for the days after, or RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING in SQL), never a rows frame, which also counts the other rows of the same date unless it runs over one row per key and date. The model writing the instruction reads the rule too. In Genie rounds 19, 20 and 25 the uplift notebook built its prior-order features with a rows frame, so a second order on a day read the first one as its history, the leakage guard stopped the first run, and Genie Code rebuilt its windows each time; a live check on serverless gave the rows frame 30 and the range frame 10 for the same order.

A Genie Code join uses a list of key names only when every key has that name on both sides, otherwise an explicit condition that drops the other side's key; before a join it renames or drops every non-key column both sides hold, renames the columns of a frame joined to itself or to its own aggregate first, and in SQL qualifies every column read after a join with its table alias, so each column name exists once after the join. In Genie round 25 a network notebook joined on [recipient, d_date] after renaming d_date to first_gift_date on one side and failed with UNRESOLVED_USING_COLUMN_FOR_JOIN; in rounds 7 and 8 three notebooks failed with AMBIGUOUS_REFERENCE on a column both sides of a join held.

Every serverless job task Inspire creates runs once: JobLauncher (the agent's own Inspire run, the persistent job of every Genie Code notebook and its scheduled-run plan) and the Inspire App's Inspire, demo-data and bundle jobs (the inspireTaskCompute helper in server.js and demoDataPipeline.js, and databricks.yml) set disable_auto_optimization, because serverless otherwise reruns a failed task up to twice even with no retry setting. The SDK of serverless environment 1 (0.20.0, where App runs execute) has no such field, so JobLauncher builds the task from a Task subclass whose as_dict adds it; a task on a cluster keeps the plain Task and the cluster's retry setting. In the 21 days of v1.3.0 live runs the platform retried 5 failed Inspire runs, among them a Generate that failed 3 times under one session and a Discover whose retry ran 48.7 minutes until it was canceled, and rescued none of them (4 failed, 1 canceled, 81.8 minutes in all); across the workspace 0 of 86 retried runs succeeded.

A Genie Code loop over itertuples() reads each row's fields as row.name, never row['name']: its rows are named tuples, and a field read by name in brackets raises TypeError; DataFrame columns are still read as x_pdf['name']. In Genie round 26 a freight anomaly notebook read its itertuples() rows by name in brackets while building its row text, and its first run stopped on TypeError: tuple indices must be integers or slices, not str.

toPandas() turns each value of an ARRAY or MAP column into a numpy array or a dict, and NULL into None, so a Genie Code notebook reads one as np.asarray(x if x is not None else [], dtype=float), counts it with len() and never tests it as a condition (if x, x or []), and replaces inf with NaN in the numeric columns only (select_dtypes('number')), because a replace over the whole frame compares each array value. In Genie round 26 a Pareto notebook whose instruction returned per-item ticket arrays failed twice with The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous: first on row.other_paid_values or [], then on a replace of inf over the whole frame; pandas 3.0.5 reproduces both failures and the numeric-only replace.

run_use_case() passes each Genie Code step, as arguments, every value it reads that an earlier step computed, since a name local to run_use_case() or to another step does not exist inside a step; the Platform Rules and the AGENTS.md file Inspire writes for Genie Code both say so. Every build step became a function with the short card and Run controls layout, so a value one step computes reaches another only as an argument. In Genie round 26 a Pareto notebook passed its per-unit minimum m to its halo test but not to its text step, and its third run failed with NameError: name 'm' is not defined after 5.8 minutes.

Genie Code writes every number in row text with one formatter, fmt_num, that rounds to 3 significant figures before it picks the K, M or B suffix, writes a whole result with str(int(x)) and strips trailing zeros only from text that has a decimal point; run_use_case() asserts 8 boundary cases before any step builds text (109.96 gives 110, 999.6 gives 1K, 1060 gives 1.06K, 250000000 gives 250M, 0.5 gives 0.5, -120.4 gives -120), and a ratio carries its unit: x for a multiple, % for a share of at most 1 multiplied by 100. All 40 Genie Code notebooks of rounds 20 to 27 wrote some numbers wrong: 36 cut the trailing zero of a whole number (110 as 11, 120 as 12, 100,000 as 1K, 250M as 25M) and 4 picked the suffix before rounding (999.6 as 1000) or kept zeros (0.5 as 0.500); a freight reason read 'Ship cost is 23.5 of sales price' for a ship cost 23.5 times the sales price.

A statistical result is never a data quality flag: a finding that is not significant, below a cutoff or without a planned change keeps data_quality_flag 'ok', says so in its top reasons and is Monitor; the flag holds only a row's own input problems and the flag the rules set on every row when a run-wide check fails. Inspire's acceptance text for group comparisons told the instruction to flag a non-significant finding 'not significant', against its own stop text and the column contract, so in Genie round 27 a Pareto flagged 14,397 of its 53,268 rows 'not significant', a network notebook flagged the 55 senders it could test the same way, and no row of either kept 'ok'.

rank puts the rows that pass the use case's decision test first, then the other rows whose data_quality_flag is 'ok', then the flagged rows, each group by expected impact, so a row without enough evidence never outranks a row with it. In Genie round 27 a network notebook ranked 153 senders flagged 'too few closed recipients' above the 55 senders with enough closed recipients to test, and an uplift and a lapse notebook ranked their 2,708 and 46 flagged rows among their unflagged ones, the first at rank 3,271 of 12,591 and the second at rank 230 of 27,314.

The Run controls cell's inspire_main() copies everything run_use_case() prints and exits with the outcome line first, then a blank line, 'Printed log of this run:' and that log, capped at 100,000 characters with its first fifth and last four fifths kept; the notebook that launched the tagged job run exits with 'Job run finished: <outcome>. Results table: <table>. Run: <link>' followed by the job run's log, a job run still running exits with its wait and link, and Genie Code never calls dbutils.notebook.exit in its own cells. A cell that calls dbutils.notebook.exit loses its printed output in a job run, as a probe job proved, so in Genie round 28 no readiness value, metric or summary of the 5 notebooks was visible in their job runs, and the two all-Monitor results could not be explained from the run.

A test of one unit, such as a sender, a node or an item, is gated only by its per-unit minimum, never also by the size of a group it belongs to: groups with fewer than min_group_rows rows are left out of the group findings only, each entity inside them is still scored and tested on its own minimum, and readiness counts each group and unit with the same rows, filters and minimum as the step that tests it. In Genie round 28 a network notebook's readiness counted cohorts of 30 senders with one closed edge while its test step needed cohorts of 30 senders with m closed edges, so readiness passed, 0 of 46,353 senders were tested and every row was Monitor.

data_quality_flag is never NULL: Genie Code sets it on the final frame, after its last merge and before the rank step, so a row a merge left without a flag gets the reason its inputs are missing. In Genie round 28 a Pareto wrote 18 items that a left merge left without a halo test with a NULL flag, a NaN value and reasons such as 'halo unknown% versus class baseline; not significant' for items that were never tested.

The last change to the write copy before spark.createDataFrame(w.to_dict('records'), schema) is w = w.astype(object).where(pd.notna(w), None), which also turns numpy numbers into Python numbers; a column assigned after it, such as from a list, makes pandas turn None back into NaN, which Spark writes as NaN and sorts above every number. A freight notebook wrote 39 NaN values in Genie round 27 and a Pareto 18 in round 28, the second after a correct replacement that it undid by rebuilding value from a list.

top_reasons holds up to 3 plain reasons, each a distinct fact about the row with its number: fewer when fewer facts apply, never a repeated reason, filler text written to reach 3, or a reason about a value the row lacks, which its data_quality_flag names instead. In Genie round 28 a lapse notebook padded rows to 3 reasons with 'limited comparable history', repeating it in 11,066 of 27,261 rows, then appended 2 more, so its rows carried 5 reasons. A reason with the same text on every row of a run that writes more than one row, such as a rate that is 0% for every item, says nothing about the row, so it is dropped from every row before the write and printed once in the log. In Genie round 32 every one of the Pareto notebook's 53,999 rows gave the reason 'solo rate 0%'.

Inspire names methods that work on every row: a per-group sample is x_pdf.sample(frac=1, random_state=seed).groupby(key).head(n), which keeps the group key and every row of a group smaller than n, never groupby(key).sample(n=...), which raises on such a group. In Genie round 28 the freight notebook followed Inspire's own groupby(key).sample(n=...), failed on a small group and had to repair and rerun.

A leakage check tests the dates each step read, never a second computation of its values: the feature step keeps on each row the latest date its window read, an outcome step the earliest, and the check stops on a row whose latest feature date is on or after its anchor date or whose earliest outcome date is on or before it, and on a training or reference window whose last day, plus the outcome horizon when its rows carry an outcome, is not before the first day of the holdout or scored window. A second computation differs on a missing history, a repeated date or a sample: in Genie round 28 an uplift check compared a NULL from its strict join with the feature step's 0, and in round 29 a freight check compared an approximate median with an exact one and a lapse check counted same-day orders twice, so three notebooks stopped runs that had no leakage. A window the closed-window choice left out of training is not a training window, so the check never tests it: in Genie round 31 an uplift check stopped on months that training had left out, and Genie Code narrowed it after its first run. A statistic the fit computes over its own window, such as a peer median, a MAD or an alert threshold, is tested on the holdout and scored rows that read it, never on the fit rows it was computed from, and a window's first and last day are the first and last dates its rows hold, never a bound the window excludes: in Genie round 33 the freight notebook's first guard tested its fit lines against the peer medians computed from them and compared a bound its window excludes, so it stopped a run that passed once the guard tested the holdout and scored lines on the dates they hold. The holdout and the scored rows are never checked against each other, since a scored row has no outcome and its features may read the days of the holdout's outcome horizon, and the scoring population is never cut to pass a leakage check: in Genie round 34 the coupon-uplift instruction checked the holdout's last date plus the horizon against the first scoring date, the first run stopped on it, and Genie Code cut the scored customers from 12,608 to 721.

Every date, as_of_date and window bound is a DATE or TIMESTAMP value. When a listed table holds its time only as a key to a date table, Inspire adds that date table with its columns to the instruction's TABLES ([GENIE-DATE-TABLES FIRED]), and Genie Code reads the date through the foreign key, never by parsing or converting the key. A reference table without a date column, and the date table of a table that has its own date column, are not added. In Genie round 29 the Pareto's TABLES listed only integer date keys, so Genie Code read 2452642 as YYYYMMDD, failed, and converted it by hand.

Training takes the anchors of every earlier window that closes before the holdout's first day (R183), at most one per entity and date, never only each entity's latest anchor, and readiness counts the positives of the fit and the holdout on those same anchors. In Genie round 29 an uplift notebook trained on each customer's latest anchor, which put every example in the holdout window, found no positive before it and stopped until it was repaired.

A join or map that adds columns to a frame reads them from a side with one row per key, aggregated to its key first or keyed by a row id made before the rows split, and the step asserts that the frame kept its row count. In Genie round 29 a freight notebook's map on repeated order numbers raised InvalidIndexError, and its next join on order and date grew 38,079 scored lines to 362,652 rows. A key that can be NULL joins on a null-safe condition, eqNullSafe in PySpark or <=> in SQL, because a grouping keeps NULL as one group while an equality condition never matches it: in Genie round 34 the Pareto notebook joined its class figures on the item class with an equality, its items without a class lost them, and its first run failed its own check that no profit rank exceeds the item count of its group. A step that needs to know which rows found a match reads a flag the other side adds before the join, F.lit(True), which is NULL on the rows without a match, never the other side's key, which is gone once it is dropped and is NULL on a row that a null-safe join matched on a NULL key: in Genie round 35 the coupon-uplift notebook dropped cd_demo_sk after joining customer_demographics, its readiness counts then read cd_demo_sk, and its first run raised UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.

More than 50 independent series or units are fit, scored or tested with groupBy(...).applyInPandas(...), in parallel where Spark holds the rows, never in a loop on the driver over event rows moved there with toPandas(). In Genie round 29 a Pareto moved 2,677,771 item-ticket rows to pandas and ran one test per unit for 107,132 units in a driver loop: its final run took 16.0 minutes and its Genie Code session 40.4 of its 45 minutes.

value is the result of the row's own entity, never a value of the group it belongs to, which gives every entity of the group the same value and rank. In Genie round 29 a Pareto gave every item of a store and class the group's concentration effect, so in all 594 groups of several items the items were ranked on nothing.

rank is built by one function, rank_rows(passes, data_quality_flag, impact, key), which takes four Series on one index and returns the ranks 1 to n as a Series on that index: the rows that pass the decision test first, then the 'ok' rows, then the flagged rows, each group by the expected impact or value descending with a missing impact last, then by the row key, the entity key followed by segment_or_item when an entity has several rows, so tied rows of one entity keep one order on every run. It sorts on data_quality_flag == 'ok' as a boolean, never on the flag text, whose alphabetical order puts a flag such as 'missing covariate' before 'ok' and one such as 'too few rows' after it, and run_use_case() asserts its result on a fixed case of six rows on a shuffled index before any step ranks rows. In Genie round 29 a lapse notebook sorted on the flag text, so 7,242 rows flagged 'missing covariate' took ranks from 1 while the worst clean row ranked 21,026th. Before the write the notebook checks the rank and stops on the first row that breaks it: ranks run from 1 to the row count without a gap or a repeat, every row that passes the decision test ranks before every row that does not, and every 'ok' row before every flagged row. In Genie round 31 a lapse notebook still sorted on the flag text, so 7,220 flagged rows ranked from 1 and an unflagged row ranked 27,314th. In Genie round 33 the coupon-uplift notebook sorted its 'ok' boolean ascending, so its 129 flagged rows ranked 1 to 129, and the gift-sender notebook sorted the flag text descending, so 51,589 senders below the test minimum ranked before the 55 it tested; neither checked before the write that every 'ok' row ranks before every flagged row. In Genie round 34 the lapse and Pareto notebooks returned their ranks on the positions 0 to n-1, which line up only on a frame whose index is 0 to n-1.

When no candidate passes acceptance, the baseline's rows carry the baseline model's own score for each entity as value and its name as method, also when the candidate scores another quantity, such as an uplift the baseline does not estimate; a baseline that does estimate the candidate's quantity writes that estimate, such as a baseline given the treatment as a feature, whose prediction with the treatment set to 1 minus its prediction with the treatment set to 0 is its uplift, so the rank, the reasons and the decision test read the quantity the use case decides on; a constant such as 0 or the class rate is never written as value. The rule is one constant that the instruction writer and Genie Code both read verbatim. In Genie round 29 the instruction writer paraphrased the fallback without that clause, and an uplift notebook wrote uplift 0.0 for all 12,608 customers. In Genie round 35 the coupon-uplift instruction wrote the baseline's reorder probability as value while its decision test read the baseline's prediction with the coupon set to 1 minus set to 0, so the notebook's 12,591 baseline rows ranked customers on a reorder probability of 0.42 to 0.55 in a use case that ranks them on lift.

A fact whose number is missing, which fmt_num writes as 'unknown', is left out of top_reasons, recommended_action and the ai_query prompt. In Genie round 29 the reasons of every Pareto row said 'unknownx class ticket'.

run_use_case() prints each step's name and elapsed seconds as the step returns, so the printed log the job run returns shows which step is slow. In Genie round 29 the Pareto's 16.0-minute run returned only its total, and the slow step had to be found by reading the code.

A Generate or Route 1 run infers the joins of the cited tables' schemas from column names, over the tables of the run's own scope and once per schema, as Discover infers them over its scan, so a regenerated Genie instruction lists the same joins and date tables as one written at Discover time; a schema the Discover scan inferred keeps the scan's joins. In Genie round 30 Route 1 regenerated 5 instructions whose joins were 'None', because only Discover inferred joins, so no date table reached TABLES.

The holdout is the most recent closed window, and training takes the anchors of every earlier window whose last day plus the horizon is before the holdout's first day, so no training label reads an outcome from the holdout's days. The leakage check stops on a training or reference window whose last day, plus the outcome horizon when its rows carry an outcome, is not before the first day of the holdout or scored window, and the scoring pattern trains on closed outcome windows whose horizon ends before the most recent closed window. In Genie round 30 an uplift notebook trained on every closed quarter, as the rule then said, so the quarter before the holdout labeled its reorders on the holdout's days; the leakage check its instruction wrote stopped the first run, and Genie Code dropped those quarters and ran again. The leakage check reads only the windows the fit and the reference use (R172).

A unit's minimum sample is the smallest sample at which either of its two extreme outcomes (such as every trial a success, or none) reaches, in the same library test, the significance level divided by the number of units with at least that sample, and at least 5. Requiring both extremes raises the minimum wherever the baseline rate is skewed: at a rate of 8% it rises from 5 to 42 trials, and units in between go untested. In Genie round 30 a network notebook first required both extremes and Genie Code corrected it after its first run.

A unit below its minimum sample keeps its row, flagged 'too few <observations>' and Monitor, with top reasons that give its own count and the minimum ('12 tickets, the test needs 21'), never a test result such as 'not significant', which only a tested unit has; the column contract of top_reasons says the same, and the acceptance and stop texts of group comparisons give 'not significant' only to a tested finding. In Genie round 30 those texts called every finding 'not significant', tested or not, and all 38,280 Pareto items with too few tickets said it in their reasons, as if a test had run on them. Only a unit below the minimum gives that count and minimum; a row the test skipped for another reason, such as a missing input its data_quality_flag names, never does. In Genie round 31 a shipping order flagged 'missing gmt offset' read '294 peer lines, the median needs 5'. The count compared with a minimum, in readiness, in the test and in a reason, is the sample the test computes on, after the test drops what it drops, never another count of the unit or group, and a test that compares two samples checks each of them: in Genie round 34, 141 of the Pareto notebook's 53,999 rows read '17 tickets, the test needs 17', because its sign test dropped the tickets tied with the class median, and the gift-sender notebook let a quarter into its prior-year comparison by its senders, so its first run raised ZeroDivisionError on a quarter with 0 closed recipients.

A share of at most 1 is multiplied by 100 and ends in '%', and a part-to-whole ratio above 1 is written as a multiple (a ship cost 23.5x the sales price), never as a percent such as '2.35K%'.
